nodes.label: Ports & Adapters Architecture Pattern
nodes.rationale: Every external dependency (database, email, rate limiter, calendar sync) sits behind an interface in ports.ts, with dev adapters (in-memory/console-logging) swapped for real ones via one line in container.ts, so no use case, Server Action, or component ever imports a concrete adapter directly.

nodes.label: createIfSlotFree method
nodes.rationale: The in-memory adapter checks-then-inserts synchronously, safe only because JS is single-threaded per request. Postgres needs either a SERIALIZABLE transaction wrapping the overlap check + insert, or (recommended) a DB-level EXCLUDE constraint using btree_gist, so double-booking is impossible even under concurrent requests — something an application-level check alone can't guarantee.

nodes.label: rescheduleIfSlotFree method
nodes.rationale: Same EXCLUDE constraint covers rescheduling: attempt the UPDATE, catch the constraint-violation error, return false.

nodes.label: btree_gist EXCLUDE constraint
nodes.rationale: A DB-level guarantee over (solicitor_slug, tstzrange(slot_start_utc, slot_end_utc)) added as a raw-SQL migration alongside the Prisma schema, making double-booking impossible even under concurrent requests.

nodes.label: SERIALIZABLE transaction (alternative)
nodes.rationale: An alternative to the EXCLUDE constraint: wrap the overlap check + insert in a SERIALIZABLE transaction.
